A gardener has planted $N = 600$ trees of a new variety of cypresses, and she wants to estimate the proportion of trees that will reach at least one meter of height after one year.

Find a lower bound for the number of trees $n$ the gardener has to measure after one year to ensure that the margin of error for the $90%$ confidence interval for the population proportion of trees that reached one meter of height is at most $0.05$.

*Hint: Use a finite population correction factor. You may also use the fact that $P(Z > 1.645) = 0.05$, where $Z∼N(0, 1)$.*

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

Consider a population of size $N = 1000$ where some individuals have a particular characteristic. Find a lower bound for the sample size $n$ required to ensure that the margin of error for the $90%$ confidence interval for the population proportion of individuals having the characteristic is at most $0.07$.

*Hint: Use a finite population correction factor. You may also use the fact that $P(Z > 1.645) = 0.05$, where $Z∼N(0, 1)$.*

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
